bull.t: Record bookings create a visible revenue pipeline
bull.b: A record job pipeline supports medium-term revenue visibility and may improve operating leverage if conversion proceeds as planned. The roughly two-month median booking-to-revenue cycle gives management a measurable path to translate demand into reported sales.

bull.t: Battery attachment is lifting revenue per installation
bull.b: Higher battery attachment increases revenue and broadens the value proposition beyond solar generation. Greater system content per customer can support stronger unit economics and create a more durable platform for storage-led growth in residential energy.

bull.t: Structural cost reductions could improve operating leverage
bull.b: Permanent expense reductions lower the revenue required to approach operating breakeven and can make future growth more profitable. If execution stabilizes, the reduced fixed-cost base should improve resilience and allow bookings growth to translate more efficiently into earnings.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn and negative equity constrain flexibility
bear.b: The company remains dependent on external financing because operations are consuming substantial cash and the capital base is negative. This reduces resilience to execution setbacks, increases refinancing pressure, and limits the ability to fund growth without further financing.

bear.t: Revenue execution remains inconsistent despite strong bookings
bear.b: Delayed installations show that bookings are not yet converting reliably into revenue, exposing the business to execution and working-capital risk. Continued quality or project-management problems could defer growth, prolong losses, and undermine confidence in the turnaround plan.

bear.t: Accounting control weaknesses increase governance and reporting risk
bear.b: Systemic recordkeeping deficiencies and prior restatements raise the risk of additional reporting errors, management distraction, and higher compliance costs. The CFO transition adds disruption while controls are being rebuilt, making execution and investor confidence more fragile.
